fact: Bowmans reports that the National Treasury and Central Bank of Kenya published the National Payment System Bill, 2026 for public consultation, with comments due 9 October 2026, to repeal the current National Payment System Act, Cap. 491A.

Bowmans describes the National Payment System Act, Cap. 491A as the current Act, which commenced in 2014 and which the 2026 Bill would repeal; it also refers to current regulations under it on suspension and revocation of licences.

The Central Bank of Kenya page states that the National Treasury and CBK developed the draft National Payment System Bill, 2026, which intends to repeal the National Payment System Act, Cap. 491A, and posted it with a comment template for consultation.

An op-ed in The Citizen says the Treasury and CBK's draft National Payment System Bill, 2026 would repeal the 2011 National Payment System Act, with public comments closing 9 October; no adoption is reported.

The CBK page states that the National Payment System Act 2011 provides the legal framework for payment systems and providers and that the National Payment System Regulations 2014 operationalise it; the page is dated only 2026 (published date used).
